doc.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Hearing the Basie band; Joe Williams elevating the blues
summary: She heard Basie whenever she could, compares Basie and Ellington's sound, and praises Joe Williams for lifting the blues into an art form.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Did you have opportunities to hear the Basie band a number of times?

Yes. Whenever I possibly could. And of course thank God for television, because we got to see quite a bit of that in the latter years. But he had such a wonderful, he and Duke Ellington both achieved a wonderful concept of an orchestral sound and a style. Now this is an incredible thing to do, because you know there are literally thousands of jazz bands and how many of them are distinctive? And he was distinctive. Now to get back to Joe Williams of course, I had heard Joe sing, you know for years and years I’d been a fan of his. And when I moved to New York I became friends with the same sort of a musical association that he had, I’m talking about social. And so I knew him largely as just a person that you sit and chat with you know. So that’s an unusual experience to have. I © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
think he’s also an amazing singer. And he took the blues out of the sin and gin era, and you know the dark, dank music halls or clubs or anything—
Yeah, the wrong side of town.
That’s what Milt was saying when I asked him about that.

Oh did he? Well then certainly my appraisal is right, because if Milt said it, it’s genuine. At any rate, Joe just elevated it to a real art form. And without its losing any of its generic sound you know. And not only that, he’s a thoroughly nice man, and he is a vocal instrumentalist. He could, what he sings could be played on a horn and start a whole new career. And he’s a charming man, a good man. I’m very fond of him and proud of him. He’s done so much for jazz.
He’s charmed us at Hamilton a few times.
